title: Chapter 103
content:
Jakyeong narrowed his eyes in fierce concentration.

He had lathered Il-hyun’s sharp jawline with rich shaving cream to clear away the dark stubble, but having zero experience with a traditional straight razor, his hands were trembling like a leaf.

Watching the hesitation, Il-hyun let out a quiet chuckle.

"You never hesitated for a second when slitting throats. Why the shaking hands now?"

Honestly speaking, putting someone in the ground felt infinitely easier.

"Don't speak. Hold still."

Jakyeong focused entirely on the task, drawing the blade across the skin in careful, rhythmic passes. He’d never considered facial hair particularly attractive. Jakyeong barely grew any himself, so shaving was an occasional chore at best, whereas Wang Han and Ryun sprouted thick scruff overnight.

Yet on Kang Il-hyun, the dark stubble looked remarkably striking, lending his aristocratic features an air of dangerous, decadent charm. Jakyeong had half a mind to leave it, but hated the thought of the man looking more sickly and drawn than he already was.

As he leaned in close to inspect the jawline, two soft knocks sounded at the door. Lunch had arrived.

Wiping the remaining foam away with a warm, damp towel, Jakyeong took in the man's face. The days spent bedridden had stripped weight from Il-hyun's broad frame, making his sharp angles appear even more severe.

After tidying the counter, Jakyeong deployed the rolling tray table over the bed and set down a bowl of warm porridge. Doctors had placed him on a strict soft-food diet, leaving plain white rice porridge as the only option on the menu.

Jakyeong set out the ceramic spoon and poured a fresh glass of water, urging him to eat, but Il-hyun simply sat back against the pillows, staring at the tray without lifting a finger.

Putting on a pitiful, wounded expression, Il-hyun tilted his head. "Aren't you going to feed me?"

Jakyeong gave him an incredulous look. His left arm was in a cast from a hairline fracture, but his right arm was perfectly functional. The man had pulled this routine for three days straight.

Jakyeong pointed a firm finger at Il-hyun's right hand.

Il-hyun lifted his chin with unyielding entitlement. "I'm left-handed."

Since when?

Jakyeong remembered vividly that the man held chopsticks, signed multi-million-dollar contracts, and even stroked his own cock with his right hand. Before Jakyeong could call out the blatant lie, Il-hyun pushed the rolling tray away like a sulking toddler and slumped back into the pillows.

Jakyeong stared in sheer disbelief. Did catching a bullet scramble his brain? He wanted to shout at the mob boss for acting so ridiculously coquettish, but swallowed the urge.

Letting out a heavy, defeated sigh, Jakyeong pulled the chair closer and dragged the tray back.

"Fine. Open up."

The sulking facade vanished instantly as Il-hyun smoothly sat back up. The parted lapels of his hospital gown revealed layers of pristine white gauze swathing his broad torso; though his wounds were closing remarkably well, his discharge was still a ways off.

Jakyeong scooped up a spoonful of warm porridge, blew on it gently to cool the steam, and held it out.

"Say ah."

Il-hyun parted his lips, taking the spoonful in. A drop of broth caught on the corner of his mouth, which he licked away with slow, deliberate leisure, his dark eyes fixed on Jakyeong's face.

Ah... I'm craving something else entirely.

Jakyeong pretended not to hear the low mutter, scooping up another spoonful. Il-hyun stared at him with such hungry, unblinking intensity that it felt like he was devouring Jakyeong's face rather than the rice in his mouth.

Catching the wicked smirk curling the corners of Il-hyun's lips, Jakyeong sighed. "Are you five years old...?"

Despite the grumbling, the sheer absurdity of the scene drew a soft, helpless laugh from Jakyeong’s lips. He patiently fed him every last drop, helped him rinse and wash up, and rewarded him with a light kiss on the lips.

Time slipped by with surprising ease inside the quiet room.

In the afternoon, Park Tae-soo arrived. The stoic black-ops veteran had broken into a rare, beaming smile the morning Il-hyun first opened his eyes—the happiest expression Jakyeong had ever seen on the man.

While Tae-soo delivered his daily corporate briefings, Jakyeong stepped outside into the quiet corridor.

Passing staff and security details bowed with familiar deference. Word around the corporate grapevine was that Chairman Kang’s funeral had been postponed indefinitely on executive orders until Il-hyun recovered enough to preside as chief mourner. The board of directors had unanimously backed the decision.

Furthermore, prosecution authorities were preparing to summon Il-hyun for testimony regarding the "terrorist attack" the moment he cleared physical therapy. Public opinion, however, leaned heavily in Il-hyun's favor—the media slamming prosecutors for dragging a grieving, critically wounded victim through grueling interrogations.

When Tae-soo concluded the meeting and bowed out, Jakyeong stepped back inside. Golden twilight was bleeding across the western sky.

"Tae-soo is waiting downstairs with a car," Il-hyun said quietly. "Go home and sleep in a real bed tonight."

Jakyeong’s brow furrowed in confusion. "Why...?"

"You can't keep sleeping in a hospital chair. Your leg isn't fully healed either."

Jakyeong pointed toward the executive lounger beside the wall. Even though he’d insisted the pull-out sofa was more comfortable than most hotel beds, Il-hyun kept nudging him to leave. Feeling pushed away pricked a small, irrational pocket of hurt.

Determined not to budge, Jakyeong remained seated, ignoring the request.

Faced with that unyielding stubbornness, Il-hyun surrendered with a quiet sigh, sending Tae-soo a text to dismiss the convoy for the night. Only then did Jakyeong’s face brighten.

"Then... want to sleep here with me tonight?" Il-hyun asked, patting the edge of the VIP mattress.

It wasn't a standard single, but squeezing two full-grown men onto the mattress was tight. Jakyeong worried about jostling the surgical incisions in his sleep, but sensing the hesitation, Il-hyun shifted his frame closer to the railing, clearing a narrow berth.

Jakyeong climbed onto the sheets, resting his head on Il-hyun's uninjured shoulder.

"Does it hurt?"

"Not at all."

"Can I really sleep like this?"

"Be my guest. You can climb on top of me if the squeeze is too tight."

Catching the filthy double entendre a beat too late, Jakyeong scowled, burying an elbow into his ribs. "Is that all you ever think about?"

"Try having someone like you for a lover. Let's see if you can keep your mind clean."

Il-hyun reached out with his right arm, gently stroking Jakyeong’s dark brown hair. His fingers drifted down to the nape of his neck, broad palm coming to rest flat against Jakyeong’s back in slow, soothing pats.

A heavy, comforting warmth settled over Jakyeong's eyelids.

"President Kang..." he murmured, his voice slurred with encroaching sleep.

"Hm?"

Jakyeong hesitated, needing to clear the knot in his chest before the darkness pulled him under.

"I'm sorry..."

"For what?"

"Your father..."

He trailed off. Even though the old monster had passed away in the ICU, Jakyeong was the one who had buried an axe in his skull.

"He died because he courted death," Il-hyun replied smoothly, his tone remarkably flat. "Not because of you. Don't let it weigh on your mind."

The large hand rhythmically patting his back slipped beneath Jakyeong’s shirt, calloused fingers smoothing over warm, bare skin. Jakyeong stiffened slightly at the contact.

Il-hyun buried his face into the crook of Jakyeong’s neck, taking a deep, intoxicating breath. His hand tightened over the curve of Jakyeong's waist, reining in the dark, hungry arousal burning in his blood by focusing on the cold reality of Chairman Kang's demise.

In truth, the patriarch's death had solved every single strategic headache in one stroke. If taking dark pleasure in his father's murder made him a soulless monster, so be it. And as for Jakyeong’s lingering guilt... Il-hyun had every intention of leaving that emotional wound wide open.

If guilt was the leash that kept the feral assassin bound to his side, he would exploit every last drop of it to ensure Lee Ja-kyeong never left his grasp.

Hiding the calculated malice behind a mask of tender warmth, Il-hyun smiled against his skin.

"Enough talking. Go to sleep. You look exhausted."

Jakyeong gave a faint, compliant nod, his heavy lids surrendering to the fatigue. Wary of aggravating the surgical stitches during the night, he carefully rolled onto his side, facing outward.

Il-hyun's warm breath ghosted against the back of his neck, soft lips pressing a tender kiss behind his ear.

A low, gravelly whisper floated through the dark:

I care for you so much. I've fallen completely in love with you.

Even drifting through the hazy fog of sleep, every syllable resonated with crystal clarity in Jakyeong's heart.
Conducting her morning surgical rounds, Dr. Kang Yu-jung stepped into Il-hyun’s private suite and stopped dead in her tracks.

The attending nurses behind her exchanged startled, flustered glances. Excusing the staff with a wave of her clipboard, Yu-jung stepped up to the bed just as Il-hyun cracked an eye open.

Curled tightly beside him like a sleeping kitten was Lee Ja-kyeong, one hand clutching the fabric of Il-hyun's hospital gown in a firm grip.

Yu-jung stood speechless, taking in the sight.

"Get out," Il-hyun mouthed in a silent whisper, gesturing toward the door. "Come back later. He's still sleeping."

Watching her ruthless, cold-blooded brother lower his voice to a faint murmur out of fear of disturbing someone's rest, Yu-jung shook her head with an incredulous click of her tongue.

Discovering that the gentle heir Jang Yi-an was a counterfeit had been a shock; learning the boy had arrived in Korea on a contract to assassinate Il-hyun had been even more staggering. Yet the most mind-boggling revelation was that Il-hyun had unmasked the hitman and chosen to keep him in his bed anyway.

He had explicitly forbidden Yu-jung from ever letting on that she knew the truth, going out of his way to ensure Jakyeong remained completely comfortable under his roof. It was clear the man was hopelessly, irreversibly infatuated.

While she worried about the sheer volatility of the relationship, seeing her brother—a man who had spent his life severing fingers and building criminal empires—finally living like an ordinary human brought an unexpected sense of relief.

Still, watching the domestic scene unfold before her eyes was entirely surreal.

"Out. Now," Il-hyun mouthed sharply, his brow furrowing as Jakyeong stirred slightly against the sheets.

Yu-jung exhaled a quiet sigh and slipped out into the corridor, leaving the room in tranquil silence.

Il-hyun turned his gaze back down to the figure resting beside him. Seeing the way Jakyeong slept curled into a protective ball plucked at a tender, protective chord in his chest.

He drew the duvet up, tucking it over Jakyeong’s shoulders. Yu-jung had told him everything: how Jakyeong had refused to leave the ICU waiting room for ten consecutive days, sitting like a stone monument through the nights, waiting for him to wake.

Morning sunlight poured through the sheer curtains, the warmth fluttering against Jakyeong's dark lashes until his lids drifted open, revealing those rich, striking brown eyes.

Looking at the drowsy, disoriented face beside him made Il-hyun's heart tighten with affection. If I'd died on that concrete floor, I would have missed this face forever.

"Good morning," Il-hyun smiled softly. "Sleep well?"

Jakyeong buried his face right back into Il-hyun's chest, murmuring in a thick, sleep-heavy rasp, "Thirty minutes... Just thirty more minutes."

Il-hyun leaned in closer, brushing the soft strands of hair from Jakyeong’s forehead. The moment his fingers smoothed over the crown, Jakyeong burrowed deeper into his embrace.

The feral stray had officially become a house cat.
